thread:
alex: Heads-up — new Dedicated proposal from AcmeCorp. They want 24/7 low-latency for chat (avg 120ms p50), but traffic is spiky with daily 3h peaks. Need a recommended commit size + fallback plan. cc @martha
martha: Thanks Alex. They signed a 12mo contract, willing to pay for committed throughput if we can guarantee <150ms p95. They send telemetry: peak qps ~4800 during spikes, steady ~600.
jordan: Quick cost note: H100 pool is ~1.8x A100 on cloud list price; committed discounts change that. Spot/eviction risk differs by region.
priya: Suggestion: split into a baseline commit + burst buffer. Baseline covers steady + 95th percentile non-peak. Burst uses reserved burst tokens + spot fallback on lower-cost hardware.
sam: Operational concerns: if we route bursts to spot, preemptions could spike latency. Need a graceful degradation policy (e.g., accept degraded response quality or route to smaller context models).
olivia: We have a recent runtime perf profile for the models they use (LlamaX-70B). Per-GPU throughput numbers: H100 ~900 rps (128-token avg), A100 ~520 rps.
alex: Ok. Basic calc: steady 600 qps => 600/900 ~0.67 H100 GPUs. Peak 4800 => 4800/900 ~5.33 H100 GPUs. If baseline commit = steady + 30% headroom => 780 qps => ~0.87 => 1 GPU. That feels low.
priya: Right, single GPU baseline is risky because of burst length. Better to size baseline for typical 95th non-peak (they reported 1400 qps outside daily storms). 1400/900=1.56 => 2 H100 GPUs baseline. Then allow burst pool of 4 GPUs (on-demand/reserved mixed) to cover full peak.
jordan: Cost sensitivity: contract tiers: commit of 2 H100s monthly vs 6 during peak. Wholesale cost delta large. If we commit only 2, they pay less; but their SLA demands make us liable if we can’t meet p95. We can use scheduled autoscaling + burst credits.
martha: Customer preference: predictable invoice, so they'd prefer higher commit if we can guarantee failover routes. They asked about an explicit outage fallback to smaller model with same SLA.
sam: Fallback idea: route to quantized 8-bit variant on A100 spots for non-critical requests and tag responses with low-confidence header. That reduces cost but increases error rate. Need engineering to add header and rollout plan.
olivia: Implementation: add routing policy: primary H100 commit pool; secondary pool = reserved A100 burst (2 GPUs) + spot autoscale up to 4 A100s; tertiary = quantized-8bit LlamaX on CPU/GPU for long tails. Policy example:
```
policy:
  primary: 2x H100 reserved
  burst_reserved: 2x A100
  burst_spot_max: 4x A100_spot
  fallback_model: llamaX-70B-8bit
  sla_target: p95 < 150ms
```
priya: We should also model throttling latency: when spot preempt happens, routing rebalancing takes ~8-12s currently. That shows up as latency spikes for a subset of requests. We can smooth using request queuing + progressive shed (slow requests become async).
ajex: (typo) alex: +1. Also suggest regional split: move baseline into eu-west for customer region and keep burst in us-west cheaper spots. But cross-region latency could break p95.
jordan: Regional egress cost for cross-region routing adds ~$0.02 per request at their qps — multiplies quickly. Need to keep compute in-region.
priya: So commit sizing recommended: baseline = 2 H100s in eu-west (covers 95th non-peak). Burst plan = 4 A100s spot + 2 A100 reserved in same region. Contract ask: commit 2 H100 + option to convert reserved A100 to committed if customer accepts higher monthly.
martha: I'll run this proposal by the customer: 2x H100 committed + optional burst package (2 reserved A100 + spot up to 4). Need a simple ROI line to justify extra reserved burst.
jordan: ROI quick calc: incremental committed A100 per month vs on-demand + spot variance. If burst only used 10% of month during storms, paying on-demand might be cheaper; if >25% then reserved wins.
olivia: Ops checklist before we promise: pre-warming images on reserved A100s, KV-cache warmup strategy, rollout automation for fallback model, monitoring alert for preemption-induced latency.
sam: Also add canary for 2 weeks with synthetic traffic (ramp to peak) and SLO observability. If p95 breaches, auto-escalate to human oncall.
alex: I'll create a short runbook and synthetic traffic script. @devops-bot please schedule a canary job for next Tue 03:00 UTC.
devops-bot: Scheduled job "acmecorp-dedicated-canary" for 2028-05-03T03:00:00Z. Reminder 60m before.
martha: Thanks everyone — will update customer. Alex, share the runbook and cost slides when ready. :thumbsup:
